translations.source_sense_description: Sport: Abfolge wechselseitiger Schläge (meist beim Boxen oder Rugby)

glosses: A baseball game in which many runs are scored, especially by home runs.

examples.text: The game turned into a 15-9 slugfest.

In a World Series that has come to be defined by the unpredictable and unexpected, it was only fitting that one night, after a lights-out pitchers’ duel between the heretofore unremarkable Alex Wood and Charlie Morton, a slugfest would unfold that sent the Cy Young Award winners Clayton Kershaw and Dallas Keuchel to early exits.

glosses: A game or match in which heavy blows are exchanged.

examples.text: Nadal is supposedly the alpha male in any slugfest. But Rosol's forehand shots were being sent towards the Majorcan at 93mph plus, and his was the fastest serve at 134mph.
The championship bout was a slugfest; both boxers were bloodied.

But while Roger Federer and Serena Williams were bludgeoning their opponents off the main court in a combined 126 minutes, the fans looking for a fantastic match stuffed into Armstrong Stadium next door to watch a mesmerizing slugfest between seventh-seeded Gaël Monfils of France and Juan Carlos Ferrero of Spain.

glosses: A tough, heated contest.

examples.text: Lakers win slugfest over Clippers
There isn’t much reason to be optimistic about thoughtful dialogue in this general election. Both sides are girded for a negative, no-holds-barred slugfest.

The race descended into a brutal slugfest as the leading candidates, the author-turned-venture capitalist J.D. Vance, the former state treasurer Josh Mandel and a self-funded businessman, Mike Gibbons, entered the final weekend before Tuesday’s primaries accusing one another of being insufficiently right-wing or disloyal to the man in Mar-a-Lago.

The possible reversal of fortunes comes as Ukraine is preparing to mount a broader counteroffensive, aiming for a dramatic breakthrough in a war that has settled into a grueling slugfest, with much blood spilled but little ground gained.

glosses: An argument or disagreement, a failure to agree.

examples.text: A "who-does-what" labour dispute at Swindon works during April led to a stoppage of work on the construction of the new 0-6-0 Type 1 diesel-hydraulic locomotives of the D9500 series and work had not been resumed as we closed for press.

glosses: Verbal controversy or disagreement; altercation; debate.

examples.text: Addicted more / To contemplation and profound dispute.

glosses: to contend in argument; to argue against something maintained, upheld, or claimed, by another.

examples.text: "Now, though thy thoughts are green and tender, as becometh one so young, yet are they those of a thinking brain, and in truth thou dost bring back to my mind certain of those old philosophers with whom in days bygone I have disputed at Athens, and at Becca in Arabia, for thou hast the same crabbed air and dusty look, as though thou hadst passed thy days in reading ill-writ Greek, and been stained dark with the grime of manuscripts."

glosses: to make a subject of disputation; to argue pro and con; to discuss

examples.text: Some residents disputed the proposal, saying it was based more on emotion than fact.

glosses: to oppose by argument or assertion; to controvert; to express dissent or opposition to; to call in question; to deny the truth or validity of

examples.text: to dispute assertions or arguments
to seize goods under the disputed authority of writs of assistance

glosses: to strive or contend about; to contest

examples.text: to dispute the possession of the ground with the Spaniards

glosses: to struggle against; to resist

examples.text: Dispute it [grief] like a man.

translations.source_sense_description: verbal: erregte Unterhaltung über ein Thema, meist in Form einer Erörterung, Diskussion

glosses: Discussion plus ou moins vive à propos d’opinions, d’intérêts.

examples.text: Dispute de mots : Débat qui tient à un malentendu sur les définitions des choses.
Avoir dispute ensemble, contre quelqu’un.

Hervé connaissait, pour y avoir passé comme les autres, l'ordre et la marche de ces disputes, et n'étant pas tenté de mettre le doigt entre l'arbre et l'écorce, il avait eu soin de se tenir à distance.

C’était un ivrogne qui, battant le trottoir et se heurtant aux arbres, menait une longue dispute avec les êtres de son rêve auxquels il donnait généreusement la parole, et qu’il accablait ensuite sous de grands gestes et des mots impérieux.
Une longue et subtile dispute.

– La dispute est d’un grand secours, sans elle on dormirait toujours, dit la Sage, histoire de reprendre la conversation.
– La Fontaine, « Le Chat et le Renard », livre IX, fable 14, vers 9 et 10, dit Kangourou, qui a sorti la bonne fiche de sa sacoche.

glosses: Altercation violente, querelle.

examples.text: Il m’était impossible de rester cinq minutes avec elle, qu’une dispute —qui se terminait invariablement par des violences de sa part— n’éclatât aussitôt.
Une dispute éclata dans la rue. — Il cherche dispute à ses voisins.

glosses: Discussion, débat publics qui se faisaient dans les écoles, pour trancher les questions de théologie, de philosophie, etc.

examples.text: Je crois que les disputes théologiques sont à la fois la farce la plus ridicule et le fléau le plus affreux de la terre, immédiatement après la guerre, la peste, la famine et la vérole.
J’ai admiré son esprit de dispute, capable de le faire se retirer de son propre avis, aussitôt qu’il voyait son contradicteur prêt à s’y ranger.
